findings.evidence: Lines 39 and 44 impose global hypotheses/conclusions, while `RegularReparametrization.lean:111-127` exists solely to extend interval speed through `projIcc` before applying the lemma at line 132.
findings.fix: State the theorem using `ContinuousOn v (Icc a b)` and `∀ t ∈ Icc a b, 0 < v t`, construct any needed extension internally, and drop the global `invFun`/`StrictMono` conclusions in favor of interval inverse properties.
findings.issue: The interval inverse API requires `Continuous v` and positivity on all of `ℝ`, although every advertised result concerns `[a,b]`; its sole caller consequently manufactures a clamped global extension at lines 111–127.

findings.evidence: The signatures occur at lines 86 and 215; `hgamma : ContMDiffOn ... (Icc a b)` is immediately adjacent, and Mathlib's `ContMDiffOn.contMDiffAt`/`MDifferentiableOn.mdifferentiableAt` APIs recover actual differentiability wherever the set is a neighborhood.
findings.fix: Replace `hmdiff` in both public theorems by `MDiffAt gamma a ∧ MDiffAt gamma b` (or equivalent endpoint hypotheses) and derive the interior cases from `hgamma` using that `Icc a b` is a neighborhood of points in `Ioo a b`.
findings.issue: `hmdiff : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, MDiffAt gamma t` is stronger than needed in both this theorem and the duplicate signature at line 215: `hgamma` already yields `MDiffAt` at every interior point, so only endpoint differentiability is additional data.

summary: The inverse lemma and both reparametrization theorems impose unnecessarily global or pointwise assumptions instead of the natural compact-interval hypotheses.
